## ECTHYMA GANGRENOSUM
Ecthyma gangrenosum lesions commonly begin as painless red macules which
rapidly evolve into areas of induration that develop into pustules and-or
bullae. Ultimately, these become gangrenous ulcers. Ecthyma lesions
typically progress rapidly within 12 to 18 hours. They are often associated
with Pseudomonas aeruginosa bacteremia, especially in neutropenic patients.
Recommend blood cultures and culture of skin exudates.
#Inpatient Infectious disease consult is suggested.
Consider combination therapy in patients with severe infections.
Treat for 7 days.
## Preferred treatment
[Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 gm IV q6h ($$) [R]](psjizid-pip-taz-4-5gm-iv-q6h-ne-extinf-ci-cefep-metro)
[Ciprofloxacin 400 mg IV q8h ($) [R,DI]](psjizid-ciproflox-400mg-iv-q8h)
[Gentamicin 5 mg/kg IV q24h ($) [R,O]](psjizid-gentamicin-5-mg-kg-iv-q24h)
## Alternative for severe infections
[Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 gm IV q6h ($$) [R] < AND > gentamicin](orz-set-abx-pip-tazo-4-5-gm-iv-q6h-gent-5mg-iv-qd)
5 mg/kg IV q24h ($) [R,O]
